gaps: No glyph pixels were successfully inspected in this turn. Academia Sinica labels a Chu manuscript example, but its image endpoint was inaccessible; Commons’ exact file page, SVG, and API were also inaccessible. Do not select either image or assert its pictorial details from metadata.

The Academia Sinica record gives script categories but not a dated artifact or a chronology establishing that the displayed Chu graph is the earliest attestation. Exact earliest date and semantic transition from stool to table remain unresolved.

Shuowen and Duan Yucai support a traditional furniture/pictograph analysis, but the object identification and graphic interpretation remain source assertions rather than independently verified paleographic conclusions.
The queried official Unihan pages for 几 U+51E0 and 幾 U+5E7E both failed to open. Local rows say kMandarin 几 jǐ and 幾 jǐ, but no verified official click-through record was obtained.

The supplied Baxter–Sagart local rows were checked for both characters and preserve the distinction between 几 ‘stool’ *C.kr[ə]jʔ and 幾 ‘small; almost’ *kəj / ‘few; how many’ *kəjʔ. The upstream table page was not verified externally. These rows do not establish a phonetic role.

This turn found no primary source establishing when simplified 几 began to spell the quantity word traditionally written 幾, nor a documented semantic path from the furniture word 几 to those quantity meanings. Keep graph borrowing/spelling distinct from the independent furniture graph.
No sound component is proposed for 几; the graph’s own reconstructions and readings do not make it a phonetic component.
